metadata.title: Matching Pursuits with Time-Frequency Dictionaries
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Time-Frequency Atom
nodes.statement: A time-frequency atom is $g_\gamma(t) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{s}} g\!\left(\frac{t-u}{s}\right) e^{j\xi t}$ with index $\gamma = (s, u, \xi) \in \Gamma = \mathbb{R}^+ \times \mathbb{R}^2$, generated by scaling, translating, and modulating a real window $g \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$.
nodes.statement_clean: A time-frequency atom is built by scaling, translating, and modulating a real window function g.

nodes.name: Dictionary
nodes.statement: A dictionary $\mathfrak{D} = (g_\gamma)_{\gamma \in \Gamma}$ is a family of unit-norm vectors in a Hilbert space $H$ ($\|g_\gamma\| = 1$). Let $V$ be the closed linear span of the dictionary vectors.
nodes.statement_clean: A dictionary is a family of unit-norm vectors in a Hilbert space.

nodes.name: Complete Dictionary
nodes.statement: A dictionary $\mathfrak{D}$ is complete in $H$ if and only if $V = H$, i.e. finite linear expansions of dictionary vectors are dense in $H$.
nodes.statement_clean: A dictionary is complete when its finite linear expansions are dense in the Hilbert space.

nodes.name: Residue and Structure Book
nodes.statement: Given $f \in H$ and a chosen $g_{\gamma_0}$, decompose $f = \langle f, g_{\gamma_0}\rangle g_{\gamma_0} + Rf$, where $Rf$ is the residue, orthogonal to $g_{\gamma_0}$. Iterating yields a structure book $(\langle R^n f, g_{\gamma_n}\rangle, \gamma_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Each iteration produces an inner-product / index pair stored in the structure book.

nodes.name: Choice Function
nodes.statement: A choice function $C$ associates to any subset $\Lambda$ of $\Gamma$ an index $\gamma_0 = C(\Lambda) \in \Lambda$. It selects, at each iteration, an atom $g_{\gamma_n}$ in the set $\Lambda_0 = \{\beta \in \Gamma : |\langle f, g_\beta\rangle| \geq \alpha \sup_{\gamma \in \Gamma} |\langle f, g_\gamma\rangle|\}$, with optimality factor $0 < \alpha \le 1$.
nodes.statement_clean: A rule for selecting one near-optimal atom from the candidate set at each step.

nodes.name: Correlation Ratio
nodes.statement: The correlation ratio of $f \in H$ with respect to $\mathfrak{D}$ is $\lambda(f) = \sup_{\gamma \in \Gamma} \frac{|\langle f, g_\gamma\rangle|}{\|f\|}$, and $I(\lambda) = \inf_{f \in H} \lambda(f)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Maximum normalized correlation between f and any dictionary atom.

nodes.name: Coherent Structure
nodes.statement: A signal $f$ has $m$ coherent structures with respect to $\mathfrak{D}$ if the first $m$ vectors $(g_{\gamma_n})_{0 \le n < m}$ chosen by the matching pursuit have higher than average correlation with the residue: $\tilde\lambda(R^n f) > E(\tilde\lambda(R^n W))$ for $0 \le n < m$ and $\tilde\lambda(R^m f) \le E(\tilde\lambda(R^m W))$.
nodes.statement_clean: Coherent structures are the early atoms whose correlation exceeds the noise expectation.

nodes.name: Dictionary Noise
nodes.statement: Dictionary noise refers to a stochastic process $R^\infty W$ that the residues $R^n f$ converge to (in distribution) as $n$ increases, with energy uniformly spread across the dictionary; for a Gabor dictionary applied to white noise it is stationary.
nodes.statement_clean: The asymptotic incoherent residual that matching pursuit approaches.

nodes.name: Admissible Set
nodes.statement: A subset $\Lambda \subset \Gamma$ is admissible and associated to $f \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ if $\Lambda = \{\beta \in \Gamma : |\langle f, g_\beta\rangle| \geq \alpha \sup_{\gamma \in \Gamma} |\langle f, g_\gamma\rangle|\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Admissible sets are the candidate index sets used by the choice function.

nodes.name: Covariant Choice Function
nodes.statement: A choice function $C$ is covariant if and only if for any admissible $\Lambda$, $C(\Lambda) = (s_0, u_0, \xi_0)$ implies $C(\Lambda_{(a,b,c)}) = (s_0/a, (u_0 - c)/a, a(\xi_0 - b))$, where $\Lambda_{(a,b,c)}$ rescales-translates-modulates indices in $\Lambda$.
nodes.statement_clean: Choice function commutes with the dilation/translation/modulation group action on indices.

nodes.name: Discrete Gabor Atom
nodes.statement: For $\gamma = (s, p, 2\pi k/N)$, the discrete complex Gabor atom is $g_\gamma(n) = g_s(n - p) e^{j2\pi k n /N}$, with $g_s(n) = \frac{K_s}{\sqrt{s}} \sum_{p=-\infty}^{+\infty} g\!\left(\frac{n - pN}{s}\right)$ and $K_s$ chosen so $\|g_\gamma\| = 1$.
nodes.statement_clean: Discretized periodic Gabor atom built from a Gaussian window.

nodes.name: Wavepacket Dictionary
nodes.statement: A wavepacket dictionary is a family of orthonormal bases of vectors well localized in time and frequency, computed with a quadrature mirror filter bank. Each $g_\gamma$ has $\gamma = (j, k, p)$ with $0 \le j \le \log_2 N$, $0 \le p \le 2^{-j} N$, $0 \le p \le 2^j$.
nodes.statement_clean: Family of orthonormal bases generated by quadrature mirror filter banks.

nodes.name: Wigner Distribution
nodes.statement: The cross Wigner distribution of $f, h \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ is $W[f,h](t,\omega) = \frac{1}{2\pi} \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} f(t+\tau/2) \bar{h}(t-\tau/2) e^{-j\omega \tau} d\tau$ and $Wf(t,\omega) = W[f,f](t,\omega)$.
nodes.statement_clean: The (cross) Wigner distribution: a quadratic time-frequency representation.

nodes.name: Atomic Decomposition
nodes.statement: $f(t) = \sum_{n=-\infty}^{+\infty} a_n g_{\gamma_n}(t)$ where $\gamma_n = (s_n, u_n, \xi_n)$ index a countable subset of atoms.

nodes.name: Energy Conservation of Matching Pursuit
nodes.statement: $\|f\|^2 = \sum_{n=0}^{m-1} |\langle R^n f, g_{\gamma_n}\rangle|^2 + \|R^m f\|^2$ (eq. 17).

nodes.name: Residue Recursion
nodes.statement: $R^n f = \langle R^n f, g_{\gamma_n}\rangle g_{\gamma_n} + R^{n+1} f$ (eq. 12), with $R^0 f = f$.

nodes.name: Stopping Criterion
nodes.statement: Stop when $\big\|f - \sum_{n=0}^{p-1}\langle R^n f, g_{\gamma_n}\rangle g_{\gamma_n}\big\| \le \epsilon \|f\|$, equivalently $\|f\|^2 - \sum_{n=0}^{p-1} |\langle R^n f, g_{\gamma_n}\rangle|^2 \le \epsilon^2 \|f\|^2$ (eqs. 34-35).

nodes.name: Time-Frequency Energy Distribution
nodes.statement: $Ef(t,\omega) = \sum_{n=0}^{+\infty} |\langle R^n f, g_{\gamma_n}\rangle|^2 \, W g_{\gamma_n}(t,\omega)$ (eq. 49); satisfies $\int\!\!\int Ef(t,\omega)\,dt\,d\omega = \|f\|^2$.

nodes.name: Inner Product Update Formula
nodes.statement: $\langle R^{n+1} f, g_\gamma\rangle = \langle R^n f, g_\gamma\rangle - \langle R^n f, g_{\gamma_n}\rangle \langle g_{\gamma_n}, g_\gamma\rangle$ (eq. 33).

nodes.name: Entropy of Wavepacket Coefficients
nodes.statement: $\sum_{n=1}^{N} |\langle f, g_{\gamma_n}\rangle|^2 \log_2 (|\langle f, g_{\gamma_n}\rangle|^2)$ (eq. 72) -- entropy minimized by Coifman-Wickerhauser best-basis algorithm.

nodes.name: Convergence of Matching Pursuit
nodes.statement: Let $f \in H$. The residue $R^m f$ defined by induction satisfies $\lim_{m \to +\infty} \|R^m f - P_W f\| = 0$, hence $f = \sum_{n=0}^{+\infty} \langle R^n f, g_{\gamma_n}\rangle g_{\gamma_n} + P_W f$.
nodes.statement_clean: Matching pursuit residues converge to the orthogonal projection on the orthogonal complement of the dictionary span.
conclusions: $f = \sum_{n=0}^{+\infty} \langle R^n f, g_{\gamma_n}\rangle g_{\gamma_n} + P_W f$

nodes.name: Discretization of Gabor Dictionary
nodes.statement: Let $\Delta u, \Delta \xi$ satisfy $\Delta u \Delta \xi /(2\pi) < 1$. Let $a > 1$ and $\Gamma_\alpha$ the discrete subset $\{(a^j, p a^j \Delta u, k a^{-j} \Delta \xi) : (j, p, k) \in \mathbb{Z}^3\}$. There exists $\alpha > 0$ such that $\sup_{\gamma \in \Gamma_\alpha} |\langle f, g_\gamma\rangle| \geq \alpha \sup_{\gamma \in \Gamma} |\langle f, g_\gamma\rangle|$ for all $f \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$.
nodes.statement_clean: A suitable discrete Gabor sub-dictionary preserves the optimality bound up to a constant factor.
conclusions: $\exists \alpha > 0$ such that $\sup_{\gamma \in \Gamma_\alpha} |\langle f, g_\gamma\rangle| \geq \alpha \sup_{\gamma \in \Gamma} |\langle f, g_\gamma\rangle|$ for all $f \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$

nodes.name: Positivity of Correlation Ratio Infimum
nodes.statement: Let $\mathfrak{D}$ be a complete dictionary in a finite-dimensional space $H$. Then $I(\lambda) = \inf_{f \in H} \lambda(f) > 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: On a finite-dimensional space, the worst-case correlation between any unit signal and the dictionary is strictly positive.

nodes.name: Exponential Decay of Residues
nodes.statement: Let $f \in H$. For any $m > 0$, $\|R^m f\| \le \|f\| (1 - \alpha^2 I^2(\lambda))^{m/2}$.
nodes.statement_clean: In a finite-dimensional space the matching-pursuit residue norm decays exponentially.

nodes.name: Inner Product Bound for Residues
nodes.statement: Let $h_n = \langle R^n f, g_{\gamma_n}\rangle g_{\gamma_n}$. For any $n \geq 0$ and $m \geq 0$, $|\langle h_m, R^n f\rangle| \leq \frac{1}{\alpha} \|h_m\| \|h_n\|$.
nodes.statement_clean: Cross inner products of residue components are controlled by their norms.

nodes.name: Square-Summable Sequence Limit
nodes.statement: If $(s_n)_{n \in \mathbb{Z}}$ is a positive sequence such that $\sum_{n=0}^{+\infty} s_n^2 < +\infty$, then $\liminf_{n \to +\infty} s_n \sum_{k=0}^{n} s_k = 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Square-summable positive sequences satisfy a vanishing partial-sum product property.

nodes.name: Existence of Admissible Index
nodes.statement: For any admissible set $\Lambda$ associated to a bounded and absolutely integrable $f$, the index $(s_1, u_1, \xi_1)$ defined by sup-projections is well defined and belongs to $\Lambda$.
nodes.statement_clean: An admissible set always contains a canonical extremal index.

nodes.name: Inner Product of Periodized Discrete Signals
nodes.statement: Let $f, h$ be continuously differentiable with $f(t) = O(1/(1+t^2))$, $h(t) = O(1/(1+t^2))$, and $f_d(n) = \sum_m f(n+mN)$, $h_d(n) = \sum_m h(n+mN)$. Then $\langle f_d, h_d\rangle = \sum_m \sum_q \int f(t) \bar{h}(t - mN) e^{j 2\pi q t}\,dt$ (eq. 123).
nodes.statement_clean: Discrete inner product of periodized samples expressed via Poisson formula.

nodes.name: Matching Pursuit
nodes.statement: Greedy iterative algorithm that decomposes $f \in H$ over a redundant dictionary by selecting at each step an atom $g_{\gamma_n}$ that nearly maximizes $|\langle R^n f, g_\gamma\rangle|$ and updating the residue.
nodes.pseudocode: Initialize R^0 f = f, n = 0. While ||R^n f|| > eps ||f||: select g_{gamma_n} with |<R^n f, g_{gamma_n}>| >= alpha sup_gamma |<R^n f, g_gamma>|; set R^{n+1} f = R^n f - <R^n f, g_{gamma_n}> g_{gamma_n}; n := n+1.

nodes.name: Matching Pursuit in Finite Dimensional Spaces with Subdictionary
nodes.statement: Variant for finite-dimensional $H$ that searches a finite subdictionary $\mathfrak{D}_\alpha$ via the Newton-method local refinement after a coarse search, using the update formula (eq. 33) on stored inner products.
nodes.pseudocode: Initialize inner products <f, g_gamma> for gamma in Gamma_alpha. Repeat: find tilde-gamma_n maximizing |<R^n f, g_gamma>| over Gamma_alpha; refine via Newton search; update <R^{n+1} f, g_gamma> = <R^n f, g_gamma> - <R^n f, g_{gamma_n}><g_{gamma_n}, g_gamma>. Stop when energy threshold met.

nodes.name: Back-Projection
nodes.statement: Given matching-pursuit-selected vectors $(g_{\gamma_n})_{0 \le n < m}$ and inner products $\langle R^n f, g_{\gamma_n}\rangle$, computes $P_{V_m} f = \sum_{n=0}^{m-1} x_n g_{\gamma_n}$ by solving the linear system $Y = GX$ via conjugate gradient, where $G$ is the Gram matrix of the selected vectors.
input: Stored inner products $Y = (\langle R^n f, g_{\gamma_n}\rangle)_{n}$
output: Coefficients $X = (x_n)_{n}$ giving the orthogonal projection $P_{V_m} f$
nodes.pseudocode: Form Gram matrix G = (<g_{gamma_k}, g_{gamma_l}>); solve Y = GX via conjugate gradient initialized at X_0 = 0.

nodes.name: Matching Pursuit with Discrete Gabor Dictionary
nodes.statement: Discrete implementation of matching pursuit using the real Gabor subdictionary $\mathfrak{D}_\alpha$ of size $O(N \log_2 N)$ plus Dirac and Fourier bases; each iteration costs $O(N \log N)$.
input: Discrete Gabor dictionary $g_{(\gamma,\phi)}(n) = K_{(\gamma,\phi)} g_s(n-p)\cos(2\pi k n/N + \phi)$
Subdictionary $\mathfrak{D}_\alpha$ with $\gamma = (a^j, p a^j \Delta u, k a^{-j} \Delta \xi)$, $a = 2$, $\Delta u = 1/2$, $\Delta \xi = \pi$
output: Structure book of selected real Gabor atoms
nodes.pseudocode: Compute inner products with complex Gabor atoms (eq. 64); recover phase via complex coefficients; for each iteration find tilde-gamma_n maximizing |<R^n f, g_gamma>| over Gamma_alpha; Newton-refine in neighborhood; update inner products via eq. 33; cost O(N log N) per iteration.

nodes.name: Coifman-Wickerhauser Best-Basis Algorithm
nodes.statement: Given a wavepacket dictionary providing $2^N$ orthonormal bases, finds the basis $(g_{\gamma_n})_{1 \le n \le N}$ minimizing the entropy $\sum_{n=1}^{N} |\langle f, g_{\gamma_n}\rangle|^2 \log_2(|\langle f, g_{\gamma_n}\rangle|^2)$.
output: Best orthonormal basis minimizing the entropy criterion

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1 (Convergence of Matching Pursuit)
nodes.statement: Show that $(R^n f)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ is Cauchy by combining Lemma 3, Lemma 4, and the energy conservation equation; let $R^\infty f = \lim R^n f$, prove $R^\infty f \in W$ (orthogonal complement of $V$), and identify it with $P_W f$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 1 (Positivity)
nodes.statement: By contradiction: assume there exists $(f_n)$ with $\sup_\gamma |\langle f_n, g_\gamma\rangle| \le \lambda_n \to 0$; compactness of the unit sphere yields a convergent subsequence with limit $f$ orthogonal to all dictionary vectors, contradicting completeness.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2 (Exponential Decay)
nodes.statement: Use $|\langle R^n f, g_{\gamma_n}\rangle| \geq \alpha \lambda(R^n f) \|R^n f\|$ and $\|R^{n+1} f\|^2 = \|R^n f\|^2 - |\langle R^n f, g_{\gamma_n}\rangle|^2$ to obtain $\|R^{n+1} f\| \le \|R^n f\| (1 - \alpha^2 \lambda^2(R^n f))^{1/2}$, then take the product and bound by $I(\lambda)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6 (Inner Product Identity)
nodes.statement: Substitute the periodized definitions of $f_d, h_d$, swap sums and integrals, and apply the Poisson formula $\sum_p \delta(t - p) = \sum_q e^{j2\pi q t}$ to obtain eq. 123.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2 (sketch)
nodes.statement: Use the dual frame of the Gaussian-window Gabor frame (Daubechies); bound $\sum |\langle \bar g_{j,p,k}, g_{\gamma_0}\rangle| \le K$ uniformly in $\gamma_0$ via exponential-decay estimates of $g$ and $\hat g$; conclude $\alpha \le 1/K$ satisfies eq. 62.

nodes.name: Cauchy Sequence Setup
nodes.statement: Let $h_n = \langle R^n f, g_{\gamma_n}\rangle g_{\gamma_n}$. Decompose $\|R^N f - R^M f\|^2 = \|R^N f\|^2 + \|R^M f\|^2 - 2\|R^M f\|^2 - 2\sum_{n=N}^{M-1} \mathrm{Re}\langle R^M f, h_n\rangle$ (eq. 79).

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 3 Bound
nodes.statement: Lemma 3 gives $\|R^N f - R^M f\|^2 \le \|R^N f\|^2 - \|R^M f\|^2 + \frac{2}{\alpha} \|h_M\| \sum_{n=N}^{M-1} \|h_n\|$ (eq. 80).

nodes.name: Use Energy Conservation and Lemma 4
nodes.statement: Energy conservation (eq. 17) gives $\sum |\langle R^n f, g_{\gamma_n}\rangle|^2 = \sum \|h_n\|^2 \le \|f\|^2$. By Lemma 4, $\liminf \|h_q\| \sum_{n=0}^{q} \|h_n\| = 0$, hence one can choose $q$ with $\|h_q\| \sum_{n=0}^{q} \|h_n\| \le \epsilon^2$.

nodes.name: Cauchy Estimate
nodes.statement: Combine the previous bounds to get $\|R^m f - R^{m+p} f\| \le \epsilon \sqrt{2(1 + 2/\alpha)}$ (eq. 85), proving $(R^n f)$ is Cauchy and converges to some $R^\infty f$.

nodes.name: Identify Limit with Projection
nodes.statement: Show $\langle R^\infty f, g_\gamma\rangle = 0$ for all $\gamma$ (so $R^\infty f \in W$). Since $f - R^\infty f = \sum \langle R^n f, g_{\gamma_n}\rangle g_{\gamma_n} \in V$, conclude $P_V f = \sum \langle R^n f, g_{\gamma_n}\rangle g_{\gamma_n}$ and $P_W f = R^\infty f$.

nodes.name: Initialize Residue
nodes.statement: Set $R^0 f = f$ and $n = 0$.

nodes.name: Atom Selection (loop body)
nodes.statement: While $\|R^n f\| > \epsilon \|f\|$: select $g_{\gamma_n} \in \mathfrak{D}$ such that $|\langle R^n f, g_{\gamma_n}\rangle| \geq \alpha \sup_{\gamma \in \Gamma} |\langle R^n f, g_\gamma\rangle|$.

nodes.name: Residue Update
nodes.statement: Set $R^{n+1} f = R^n f - \langle R^n f, g_{\gamma_n}\rangle g_{\gamma_n}$; record $(\langle R^n f, g_{\gamma_n}\rangle, \gamma_n)$ in the structure book; $n \leftarrow n+1$.

nodes.name: Return Structure Book
nodes.statement: Return $(\langle R^n f, g_{\gamma_n}\rangle, \gamma_n)_{n=0}^{p-1}$ and (optionally) $R^p f$.

nodes.name: Initialize Inner Products
nodes.statement: For all $\gamma \in \Gamma_\alpha$, compute $\langle f, g_\gamma\rangle$ with the complex Gabor atoms (eq. 64) using FFT-like routines.

nodes.name: Coarse Search and Newton Refinement
nodes.statement: Find $\tilde\gamma_n$ maximizing $|\langle R^n f, g_\gamma\rangle|$ over $\Gamma_\alpha$; apply Newton search in a neighborhood of $\tilde\gamma_n$ to refine the time-frequency parameters.

nodes.name: Update Inner Products
nodes.statement: Update via $\langle R^{n+1} f, g_\gamma\rangle = \langle R^n f, g_\gamma\rangle - \langle R^n f, g_{\gamma_n}\rangle \langle g_{\gamma_n}, g_\gamma\rangle$, computing $\langle g_{\gamma_n}, g_\gamma\rangle$ from the analytic formula (eq. 127).

nodes.name: Synthetic 512-Sample Signal (chirps + sinusoids)
nodes.statement: A synthetic signal of 512 samples built by adding chirps, truncated sinusoidal waves, and waveforms of different time-frequency localizations; matching pursuit with Gabor dictionary recovers two crossing chirps, localized waveforms, Diracs, and closely-spaced sinusoids in $Ef(t,\omega)$.

nodes.name: Speech Recording 'greasy'
nodes.statement: Speech recording of the word 'greasy' (5782 samples, 16 kHz). Matching pursuit with $n = 250$ Gabor atoms gives $\|R^n f\|/\|f\| = 0.169$ and reproduces low-frequency 'g', burst transition to 'ea', harmonics of 'ea', and high-frequency spread of 's' with excellent auditory quality.

nodes.name: Noisy Speech (SNR 1.5 dB)
nodes.statement: The 'greasy' signal corrupted with Gaussian white noise at SNR 1.5 dB. Matching pursuit isolates $m = 76$ coherent Gabor atoms; reconstructing from these yields a denoised signal with SNR 6.8 dB, demonstrating coherence-based denoising.

nodes.name: Wavepacket Best-Basis vs. Matching Pursuit
nodes.statement: Same 512-sample synthetic signal of Fig. 1(a) decomposed in the optimal wavepacket orthonormal basis (Coifman-Wickerhauser entropy minimization) with Daubechies-6 QMF: many signal components (including the chirps) are not clearly separated, illustrating the limits of global basis selection compared to greedy matching pursuit.

nodes.name: Connection to Projection Pursuit
nodes.statement: Matching pursuit closely parallels projection pursuit regression of Friedman and Stuetzle: both decompose by iterated near-optimal one-dimensional projections. Mathematical similarities allow Jones's convergence proof to be transposed.

nodes.name: Complexity Comparison with Best-Basis
nodes.statement: Best-basis algorithm has total complexity $O(N \log N)$, while matching pursuit per-iteration complexity is $O(N \log N)$; matching pursuit is more flexible for non-stationary signals but requires more computation than best-basis.

nodes.name: Shape-Gain Vector Quantization Analogy
nodes.statement: Matching pursuit is similar to a multistage shape-gain vector quantizer, except that inner products are not quantized and the dictionary may be infinite, suiting information-processing applications rather than data compression.

nodes.name: Adaptive Decomposition over Redundant Dictionary
nodes.statement: Find an expansion of $f \in H$ over a chosen subset of vectors selected from a redundant dictionary $\mathfrak{D}$, in order to best match the inner-product structures of $f$. The dictionary is too redundant for any orthogonal basis search to be feasible.

nodes.name: Learning High-Dimensional Dictionaries
nodes.statement: Finding strategies to optimize dictionaries in high dimensions is an open problem, sharing similar features with learning problems in neural networks. Classical algorithms such as LBG do not converge to satisfying solutions in such high-dimensional vector spaces.
